text: MUST 221/ARCH 221 Foundations of Museum Studies Credits: 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Overview: 3 Lecture Hours. Introduction to museums, cultural heritage and collections care; best practices for non-profit institutions, public engagement and the collection, preservation and exhibition of material culture; emphasis on archaeological, ethnographic, and historical collections, or other collections of cultural significance. Cross Listing: ARCH 221/MUST 221 .

MUST 421/ANTH 421 Advanced Museum Studies Credits: 3. 2 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. Overview: 2 Lecture Hours. 3 Lab Hours. Exploration of advanced topics in museum programs; preservation, research, education, outreach; development and implementation; emphasis on historical contexts, disciplinary intersections, ethical obligations and professional responsibilities; service to community, state and national interest and advancement of sciences. Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MUST 221/ARCH 221 , ARCH 221/MUST 221 , or MAST 220 ; junior or senior classification. Cross Listing: ANTH 421/MUST 421 . text: MUST 484 Internship Credits: 0 to 3. 0 to 3 Other Hours. Overview: 0 to 3 Other Hours. Provides students with the opportunity to gain practical experience in a variety of cultural heritage settings, including museums, archives, libraries, art galleries, conservation and preservation laboratories, and collection facilities. May be taken four times for credit. Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor. Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.
